 DAUPHIN COUNTY, Pa. (WHP) — The state senate does not have any more sessions ahead of Election Day, which is a week from Tuesday, and leaders on the democratic and republican side are pointing fingers at one another for the lack of progress. CBS 21 spoke with the Senate Minority Leader Jay Costa and Senate Majority Leader Joe Pittman, who both felt the opposite side is the reason that nothing was done in the sessions leading up to the midterms.
 Senator Costa told CBS 21 News that democrats main issue was minimum wage and raising that to benefit Pennsylvanians. The current minimum wage is $7.25/hour in Pennsylvania, tied for the lowest total in the country, but equal to the national minimum wage.
 Costa said that because neighboring states like West Virginia and New Jersey have much higher minimum wages, it opens the door for Pennsylvanians to travel to those states to work and make more money.
 "They go a few miles into West Virginia to do the same job," explained Costa. "They make $3000 more if they’re on the eastern part of the state living close to Philadelphia. Let’s say they go across the Walt Whitman bridge and they’re able to make $17,000 more because their rate their rate is $16 that’s a frustrating thing."
 Senator Joe Pittman told CBS 21 that republicans are open to making a deal when it comes to minimum wage, but it has to benefit everyone.
 "I’ve been very clear that we’re willing to do a thoughtful increase in the minimum wage of sit down for four years. The reality is Matt and Jay want this as a political talking point," Pittman said. "I don’t wanna come to the table and figure out a way to thoughtfully increase the minimum wage to a level that works for all of Pennsylvania as diverse this Commonwealth is."
 Other major issues included the Governor's GRID guidelines and data centers, and overall affordability issues that many across the Commonwealth face. And of course, skill games remain at the top of minds of lawmakers in the Commonwealth.
 There isn't a deal in place, but lawmakers said there has been discussion.
 "Spending hours after hours after hours drafting a document quite frankly, they did clean up some of the language that needed to be done on gaming in that title for but more importantly, implementing not only a skill game program or a gaming program, gaming reform, setting a regulatory framework as well as a tax rate, but also on the side of transportation making sure we cover those things,” Costa said.
 But republicans said it's not as easy as just picking a tax rate and running with it, there's nuance to the skill game legislation.
 "There’s a lot of moving parts to gaming. Gaming, whenever it’s done in this building often takes multiple tries multiple years," Pittman explained. "How do you get it into an age restricted environment to comply with the Supreme Court ruling how do you get the gaming control board to properly regulated and then of course, where do the resources go that are generated from the revenue?"
 Election Day is Tuesday November 3rd, and both legislators said they have priorities for afterwards. Republicans said their priority is growing the economy in the Commonwealth. Democrats said minimum wage is still issue number one on their agenda.
